I’m constantly on the move at the salon—reorganizing the clippers, chatting with clients nonstop, playing with the dogs between appointments. My coworkers joke I never shut up, and it’s true—I feel this pressure to keep talking, like silence is unbearable. My boss has pulled me aside a few times because I’ll talk over clients or rush through grooming just to keep doing more.

I feel almost too good—like everything is exciting, and I’m on top of the world for no real reason. I’ve also been a lot more into sex than usual. I’ve been flirting with clients, messaging multiple people, and hooking up more often. It’s not really like me, and it’s starting to cause drama with friends.

There was this thing that happened a while back—something pretty scary—that I don’t really like to go into. I don’t know if any of this is connected to that or if it’s just me going off the rails lately.

I know I had that car accident last year—the one where the truck almost hit me and I still get jumpy sometimes—but this feels different. It’s like someone flipped a switch and I’m just “on” all the time for no clear reason.

At the shop, I’m buzzing around nonstop, talking a mile a minute to clients about their dogs, random ideas, future plans. I can’t seem to stop talking or just sit quietly; silence feels unbearable. I barely sleep, maybe three hours, but I wake up feeling like I’ve had a full night and I’m ready to go again. I’ll clean the whole apartment at 3 a.m. or start planning a new grooming business.

I’ve also been way more into sex than usual—hooking up with people I normally wouldn’t, flirting with customers, sexting late at night. My coworkers say I’m “too much” lately, and I’ve gotten in trouble for being overly loud and inappropriate at work. It comes in this big wave, separate from the accident stuff.
D008-D018_h013.question_b:
I work as a dog groomer, so I’m used to being busy, but this is different. About a year ago I was walking home after a late shift and a guy dragged me into an alley and sexually assaulted me. Since then, it’s like my body is stuck on “on.” I’m constantly wired and on edge. I can’t relax on the couch, I pace my tiny apartment, and even when I’m exhausted my mind won’t shut off enough to sleep. It’s been this way basically every day since it happened, not coming and going in phases.

I talk a lot more now, like I just start rambling to customers or my coworkers and then realize I can’t seem to stop. I feel this restless buzz inside, like if I sit still something bad will happen. I’ve also been having a lot more sex than before—hookups with people I barely know, almost like I’m trying to prove something or numb out what happened—but afterward I feel empty, not happy. All of this has really messed with my work and I’ve had to cut back my hours.

About a year after he died, I went through this spell for almost two months where I was just “up” all the time. I barely sat still, wandering the halls, talking everyone’s ear off. One minute I’d be joking and laughing, feeling like I could run the place, and the next I’d snap at staff over nothing. I felt like I had endless energy, hardly slept, and did foolish things—trying to leave the facility alone, insisting I could drive again, even though I can’t walk well. It caused a lot of trouble here.

Then, a few months later, I crashed into a low spell that lasted around three months. I stopped wanting to go to activities or even get out of bed. I’d wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning and just lie there, mind foggy, unable to think straight. I kept thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up someday, though I wasn’t planning to hurt myself. These ups and downs seem to come in spells, not just when I’m reminded of the accident.
D008-D018_h021.question_b:
It really started after that night two years ago, when another resident wandered into my room and put his hands on me while I was asleep. I woke up terrified, and ever since then I haven’t felt like myself.

I’m always on edge now. My mood can flip in a second if someone comes up behind me or raises their voice—I’ll snap or get very worked up, then a bit later I’m just wrung out and shaky. I feel restless a lot of the time, like I can’t sit still in the common room; I pace the hallway, check my door lock over and over, and sometimes I get these urges to just walk out of the building at night even though I know it’s not safe for someone my age.

Sleep has been bad for months. I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning from bad dreams about that night and can’t get back to sleep. In the mornings my head feels thick, like I’m in a fog, and I can’t focus on simple things like reading or bingo. I don’t really care to join activities anymore. I mostly just sit and think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up one of these days, though I’m not planning to do anything to myself.

A couple months ago I hit this stretch where I felt incredible for weeks, like I was on top of the world for no real reason. Work started getting messy; I’d forget feeding schedules, miss safety checks.

Then it kind of swung the other way. For the last three months or so, it’s like somebody turned the color down on everything. I don’t really enjoy being around the animals like I used to. I wake up two or three times a night and just lie there, replaying that day at the zoo and other random things, and I can’t settle back down. I’m misplacing keys, forgetting what I went into a room for. Lately I’ve been thinking a lot about just ending it, and I’ve actually worked out how and where I’d do it. I haven’t acted on it, but it scares me that I’ve planned it out that far.
